title: Criterion for a property of morphisms to descend along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02KP, fpqc case)
statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] satisfying the following four conditions.
(0) (Invariance under isomorphism.) If $f:X\to S$ has $\mathcal P$ and $\tilde f:\tilde X\to\tilde S$ is a morphism for which there are isomorphisms of schemes $a:X\to\tilde X$, $b:S\to\tilde S$ with $\tilde f\circ a=b\circ f$, then $\tilde f$ has $\mathcal P$.
(1) (Stable under flat base change.) If $f:X\to S$ has $\mathcal P$ and $g:S'\to S$ is a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism], then the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] has $\mathcal P$.
(2) (Zariski local on the base.) If $f:X\to S$ is a morphism and $S=\bigcup_{k\in K}V_k$ is a covering of $S$ by open subschemes such that for every $k$ the restriction $f^{-1}(V_k)\to V_k$ of $f$ (a morphism from the open subscheme $f^{-1}(V_k)$ of $X$ to the open subscheme $V_k$ of $S$) has $\mathcal P$, then $f$ has $\mathcal P$.
(3) (Descent along faithfully flat morphisms of affine schemes.) If $S$ and $S'$ are affine schemes, $g:S'\to S$ is a flat and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] morphism, and $f:X\to S$ is a morphism such that the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ has $\mathcal P$, then $f$ has $\mathcal P$.
Then for every morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ and every fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] such that for every $i\in I$ the second projection $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has $\mathcal P$, the morphism $f$ has $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KP (lemma-descending-properties-morphisms, line 5407) with tau = fpqc, the direction 'each base change has P => f has P' of 'fpqc local on the base' (Definition Tag 02KO, definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310); its proof ('details omitted') goes through Topologies, Definition Tag 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering, topologies.tex line 2888) and Lemma Tag 022E (topologies-lemma-fpqc-affine, topologies.tex line 3151: an fpqc covering of an affine scheme is refined by a finite fpqc covering by affine opens of the members). Condition (0) is the standing convention of Definition 02KO ('we see (or require) that property P holds for X -> Y iff it holds for any arrow isomorphic to it').
